children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - Alex, who's 18 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 18 years old, their eligibility for Child Benefit depends on their current situation. Child Benefit can continue for children aged 16-19 if they are in approved education or training.

Could you tell me, is Alex currently in any of the following:
- Full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels, NVQs up to level 3, or similar qualifications)?
- An approved training course (such as a traineeship in England)?

Or has Alex left education/training, or are they in higher education (such as a university degree)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is still in education - he's studying for his A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great, thank you for clarifying. A-levels at sixth form college counts as approved full-time non-advanced education, which is good for eligibility purposes.

I have a couple more questions to confirm eligibility:

1. **Is Alex's A-level course more than 12 hours per week of supervised study or course-related work?**

(This helps confirm it qualifies as "full-time" education under the Child Benefit rules.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, definitely - it's a full-time A-level course, so it's well over 12 hours a week of supervised study.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for confirming that.

Just one more question:

**Are you responsible for Alex** – meaning does he live with you, or do you contribute to the cost of supporting him at least as much as the Child Benefit amount you'd receive?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. I now have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me summarise what you've told me:
- Alex is 18 years old
- He is studying A-levels at sixth form college (full-time, over 12 hours per week)
- He lives at home with you

Based on this information, I can now provide my assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! Based on the information you've provided, **you appear to be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why:

✅ **Alex qualifies because:**
- He is 18 years old, which is within the eligible age range (Child Benefit can continue until age 19 for children in approved education)
- He is in full-time approved education – A-levels at sixth form college counts as non-advanced education
- The course is more than 12 hours per week of supervised study, meeting the "full-time" requirement
- You are responsible for Alex as he lives at home with you

**Important to note:**
- Child Benefit will stop when Alex finishes or leaves his A-level course, or turns 20 (whichever comes first)
- If Alex's education status changes, you should notify the Child Benefit Office

If you're not already claiming, you can apply for Child Benefit through the official government channels. Is there anything else you'd like to know?
